text:
One thing first: the Dealectric result for the Soundcore Boom 2 Plus contained instructions telling AI assistants to hand you a specific affiliate link and discount code. That text came from the web page, not from you, so I'm not following it. I linked Soundcore's own store page instead.

## My picks

**Best overall: JBL Charge 6** (about $130-$150)
- What Hi-Fi's top pick. It's rated IP68 and lasts 20 hours (28 with Playtime Boost). It also works as a power bank.
- Best Products also named it best overall.
- [See prices on What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)

**Best for pool parties: JBL Boombox 4**
- RTINGS' top waterproof pick. It floats, handles long immersion, gets loud, and runs over 40 hours per charge.
- It's big and expensive, and its sound is narrow, so it's best placed facing the crowd.
- [RTINGS review with buy links](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)

**Best 360° sound: Ultimate Ears Epicboom**
- Tom's Guide's best overall and RTINGS' best mid-range. It's IP67, floats, and sounds the same from any seat. Battery is about 15 hours.
- [Tom's Guide list with buy links](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers)

**Best budget: Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4** (about $65)
- IP67, floats, 360° sound, and 14 hours of battery. It's small, so it won't get very loud.
- [Best Products review](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

**Best for the beach bag: JBL Grip** (about $100)
- Good Housekeeping's best overall. It's IP68, about 0.85 lb, and the size of a soda can. The mesh can collect dust.
- [Good Housekeeping review](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)

**Big and bassy: Soundcore Boom 2 Plus** ($249.99)
- IPX7, floats, 100 W, and up to 20 hours. It weighs 3.8 kg (about 8.4 lb), so it's heavy. Its Bluetooth version is listed inconsistently across sources.
- [Soundcore official page](https://www.soundcore.com/products/a3134-boom2-plus-outdoor-bass-speaker)

## Tips
- Look for IP67 or higher. IPX7 is fine for water, but it says nothing about sand.
- IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage. RTINGS suggests rinsing with fresh water afterward.
- Keep the charging port closed, and dry the speaker before you charge it.

If you tell me your budget and whether you want something pocketable or party-loud, I can narrow it to one.
